What KYC automation covers in Verkflo

KYC automation here means an agent doing the file work in a KYC review: pulling the applicant record, checking each document against your procedure, screening the name and drafting the analyst note. Your analysts keep the judgment calls, such as possible matches and high-risk approvals.

The agent works from your own document. You upload the KYC procedure, Verkflo compiles it into a spec, and each run records which version it followed. A branch such as "High risk goes to a senior reviewer" is a CEL rule your team can read: risk_rating == "High".

Business customers and their owners have their own page, KYB automation. Alert and hit work after onboarding sits under AML automation.

Who does what in a KYC review

  • The procedure

    Your KYC procedure sets the documents you accept, the screening you run, how you rate risk and when a file needs a second pair of eyes. Verkflo runs those steps in order for each customer.

  • What the agent does

    • Fetches the applicant data and risk rating from Sumsub

    • Screens the customer for sanctions, PEP and adverse media in ComplyAdvantage

    • Finds periodic reviews that are due under your risk-based schedule

    • Drafts requests for missing documents and saves them to the case folder

  • What your team decides

    • Whether a possible match is the same person

    • Approval of customers rated High risk

    • Whether a document request goes to the customer

    • What to escalate to your MLRO or compliance officer

Each one opens with example runs and the rules behind them.

  • +1↗ Periodic KYC reviewFind the reviews that are due by risk rating, refresh the file and route changes to a reviewer.
  • +1↗ PEP and adverse media reviewCompare each PEP or adverse media hit with the customer file and put the evidence in front of a reviewer.
  • +1↗ Sanctions screeningScreen counterparties before the first payment and send each possible match to a person.

Keep the KYC provider you have

Verkflo is not an identity verification service. It reads what your provider already holds: today that is Sumsub, through its API, with Veriff Coming soon. An in-house onboarding database or any other system with an API connects through Custom REST.

The Sumsub integration page lists the exact calls an agent makes, and the ComplyAdvantage integration covers screening.

    Role-based access

    Admin, Author, Reviewer and Auditor roles, scoped to each workspace.

    Each entry carries the hash of the one before it. Verifying the log recomputes the chain and flags entries that no longer match.

    Steps point to a vault path, and the key stays in the vault.

    Unsigned or stale deliveries are rejected before a run starts.

KYC automation questions

Who makes the KYC decision?

Your rules and your people. CEL rules choose the branch a run takes, and any decision your procedure gives to a person waits for a named reviewer. The model reads documents and drafts the notes.

Can we keep our existing KYC provider?

Yes. Verkflo reads from the tools you already have contracts with. Sumsub and ComplyAdvantage connect today, and other providers connect through Custom REST if they offer an API.

How is each review evidenced?

Each step, tool call and reviewer decision goes into a hash-chained audit log, tied to the procedure version in force at the time. An auditor can read the run and that version side by side.

Does it cover periodic reviews as well as onboarding?

Yes. A schedule finds the files that are due by risk rating, the agent refreshes the data and the screening, and any change goes to a reviewer. See periodic KYC review.
